rule: published artifacts stay byte-identical; corrections are appended

entries.old_statement: zeta(600 s) = 0.166 / 0.230 / 0.262, read as strong concavity of single-order impact
entries.corrected_statement: Run on data where the relationship is EXACTLY LINEAR (true slope 1.0), with heavy-tailed x and additive noise matching the real setting, the same binned log-log estimator returns 0.2558 +- 0.1374.  The published zeta values are INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM LINEAR IMPACT.  Mechanism: in low-x bins signal is far below noise, so the bin mean is noise-dominated and the curve flattens -- classic attenuation.  This is a THIRD independent reason to withdraw those numbers (ERR-HU-012: one scaling function; ERR-HU-013: mixed estimands; now: estimator bias).  It ALSO supplies an alternative mechanism for C-T20's rising psi(T) that has nothing to do with F: at low T the signal-to-noise is worse, so attenuation is stronger and the slope is lower.  NOT extended to A-S30's zeta, which uses an OUTER-region fit -- a different estimator that this null does not test.

entries.source_section_or_line: kappa-chi from the Lambda(T) exponent fit
entries.old_statement: kappa-chi = 0.2245 / 0.3786 / 0.2032, agreeing with A-S30 to 0.010-0.031, read as a settled measurement; earlier as KAPPA_MINUS_CHI_CONFIRMED_A_THIRD_TIME
entries.corrected_statement: No null was ever run on this estimator.  On synthetic data with a CONSTANT lambda -- true exponent exactly 0 -- it returns mean -0.093 with sd 0.872 and a 90 percent interval of [-1.52, +0.92], which CONTAINS every value both lanes published.  The null's noise level was chosen by hand and not calibrated to the real scatter, so this does NOT establish that kappa-chi is zero; it establishes that the estimator's null distribution AT THE REAL SIGNAL-TO-NOISE HAS NEVER BEEN MEASURED, and until it is, 'agrees with the book's band' is not a supported reading.  Cross-lane agreement is not a substitute: two lanes running similar estimators on similar data agree under the null too.

entries.old_statement: gamma = 0.373 (BTC) and 0.369 (ETH), and C-T25 leaned on their agreeing to 0.004 to build a structural argument
entries.corrected_statement: On i.i.d. signs with NO memory the same fit returns mean -0.023 with sd 0.544 and a 90 percent interval of [-0.70, +0.56], and only 21 of 40 draws produced a fit at all because the positive-lag selection often left too few points.  The null is n-INDEPENDENT: C(l) = z_l/sqrt(n) under the null, so log|C| = log|z_l| - 0.5 log n and the sqrt(n) enters only the intercept.  The LEVELS are not void -- the real C(100) = 0.083 sits about 145 standard errors from zero and the fits have r2 0.98-0.99 -- but the PRECISION is: a 0.004 difference between BTC and ETH is two orders of magnitude inside the estimator's own noise, so C-T25's structural argument must not rest on that difference.  Its other leg -- size weighting raises gamma monotonically, 3/3 -- is unaffected.
